State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Icici Lombard Ge.In.Co.Ltd vs Anita Tiwari on 23 August, 2023
Daily Order 

M. P. STATE  CONSUMER  DISPUTES  REDRESSAL  COMMISSION,                         

                              PLOT NO.76, ARERA HILLS, BHOPAL

 

 

 

                                       FIRST APPEAL NO. 12 OF 2020

 

(Arising out of order dated 26.09.2019 passed in C.C. No.557/2017 by District Commission, Indore-2)

 

 

 

ICICI LOMBARD GENERAL INSURANCE

 

COMPANY LIMITED, ICICI LOMBARD HOUSE,

 

414, VEER SAWARKAR MARG,

 

PRABHADEVI, MUMBAI THROUGH MANAGER LEGAL.                              ... APPELLANT.

 

 

 

         Versus

 

 

 

1. ANITA TIWARI

 

    W/O LATE ARVIND TIWARI,

 

    R/O KALYAN SAMPATTI COLONY,

 

    KALI BILLOD, INDORE (M.P.)

 

 

 

2. INDIA BULLS,

 

    FIRST FLOOR, 2-A&B

 

    CORPORATE HOUSE,

 

    R.N.T. MARG, INDORE (M.P.)                                                                ...   RESPONDENTS.  

 

                    

 

 BEFORE :

 

            HON'BLE SHRI A. K. TIWARI                : PRESIDING MEMBER

 

            HON'BLE DR. SRIKANT PANDEY        :          MEMBER

 

                      

 

 COUNSEL FOR PARTIES :

 

                Shri Alankar Soni, learned counsel for the appellant.

 

           Shri Sunil Nema & Shri Vivek Anand Nema, learned counsel for the respondent no.1

 

           None for the respondent no.2.

 

 

 

 O R D E R
(Passed On 23.08.2023)

 

                                The following order of the Commission was delivered by A. K. Tiwari, Presiding Member:
Challenging the order dated 26.09.2019 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Indore-2 (for short 'District Commission') in C.C.No.557/2017 whereby the District Commission has allowed the complaint filed by the complainant/respondent no.1 (hereinafter
-2-
referred to as 'complainant'), the opposite party no.2/appellant-ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company (hereinafter referred to as 'insurance company') has filed the instant appeal.
2.                Facts of the case as narrated by the complainant are that the complainant's late husband Arvind Tiwari (hereinafter referred to as 'deceased-insured') during his life time on 30.06.2014 took housing loan from the opposite party no.1-India Bulls (hereinafter referred to as 'financer'). The said loan was insured with the insurance company by two policies for 5 years term of covering the risk for a sum of Rs.3,15,000/- and Rs.3,85,000/- respectively and the financer had paid premium to the insurance company. The deceased-insured was in good health at the time of taking loan and insurance policies. Later when he fell ill he consulted the doctors at Sagar and Betma but when he could not get any relief, he consulted Dr. Suman Agrawal at Mhow, and was diagnosed some kidney ailment.  Dr. Suman Agrawal referred to him Bombay Hospital, Indore. Thereafter he underwent kidney transplant at Choithram Hospital, Indore and unfortunately died on 15.05.2017. The complainant approached the insurance company and submitted her claim.  It is alleged that thereafter on 11.01.2017 two persons from the insurance company came and advise her to give in writing to the effect that the deceased-insured was suffering from pre-existing disease in order to get claim amount at the earliest. They also
-3-
managed Dr. Suman Agrawal to write hypertension on the prescription and took Rs.25,000/- from her for settling the claim at the earliest, of which she lodged a police complaint against them on 23.06.2017. It is further alleged that despite genuine claim the insurance company rejected her claim on the ground of pre-existing disease.    The complainant therefore alleging deficiency in service on part of the opposite parties, approached the District Commission seeking relief.
3.                The opposite party no.1-financer resisted the complaint stating that the complainant had obtained housing loan from it thus liability of repayment of loan amount is of the complainant. The claim of the complainant was repudiated by the insurance company. The financer has no authority to interfere with the work of the insurance company. The deceased-insured got secured the housing loan through insurance himself. There has been no deficiency in service on part of the financer and therefore it is requested to dismiss the complaint with costs.
4.                The opposite party no.2-insurance company contested the claim on the ground that the claim was repudiated on the ground of pre-existing disease as deceased-insured was suffering from Hypertension since last 4 to 5 years. It is further submitted that at the time of proposal, the deceased-insured did not disclose the fact that he was suffering from that disease and
-4-
he was on medication for the same. Since there was violation of policy terms and conditions, therefore, the claim was not payable under 2.14 of the policy

 

terms and conditions. The insurance company has rightly repudiated the claim and while doing so, they have not committed any deficiency in service.
5.                The District Commission allowing the complaint directed the opposite party no.2-insurance company to pay claim amount of Rs.7,00,000/- to the complainant within a period of two months. It is further directed the amount towards loan paid by complainant from the date of insurance till the date of death i.e. 15.05.2017 be adjusted and interest @ 9% p.a. be paid on the balance amount from the date of repudiation i.e. 01.02.2017. Additionally, compensation of Rs.10,000/- along with costs of Rs.2,000/- is also awarded. Hence, this appeal by the opposite party no.2-insurance company.
6.                We have deeply heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record as also the impugned order. Also perused the written arguments filed on behalf of complainant/respondent no.1.
7.                Learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company argued that the impugned order passed by the District Commission is contradictory, perverse and illogical and is therefore not sustainable in the eyes of law and facts. The District Commission completely ignored the fact that the insurance being a contract of 'Uberrimae Fidae' (utmost good faith) and the
-5-
policy holder was duty bound to reveal all the relevant facts to the insurance company at the time of filling the proposal form in order to obtain insurance

 

policy, so that the insurance company determine the policy holder's eligibility for availing the insurance. The District Commission gravely erred in allowing the complaint even when the deceased-insured had violated terms and conditions of the policy and had suppressed the fact about pre-existing disease and therefore the question of deficiency in service on part of the insurance company does not arise.  He further argued that the impugned order deserves to be set-aside.
7.1              In support of his contentions, he placed reliance on the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Life Insurance Corporation of India & Ors Vs Smt. Asha Goel & Anr.
2001
ACJ 806, P. C. Chako & Anr. Vs Life Insurance Corporation of India
AIR 2008 SC 424 and the decision of the Hon'ble National Commission in Revision Petition No. 306 of 2004 Life Insurance Corporation of India Vs Shri Ghuman Singh.
8.                Learned counsel for the complainant/respondent no.1 supporting the impugned order argued that despite genuine claim of the complainant, the insurance company has committed deficiency in service in repudiating the claim on the ground of pre-existing disease.  He further urged that the insurance company failed to prove that the deceased-insured was suffering from any pre-existing disease i.e. hypertension. Even
-6-
otherwise hypertension is not a disease. He further argued that the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
8.1              In support of his contentions, he placed reliance on the decision of Hon'ble National Commission in Rasheeda Khatoon Vs Life Insurance Corporation of India III (2009) CPJ 91 (NC), Life Insurance Corporation of India & Anr Vs Ashok Manocha III (2011) CPJ 418 (NC), and the decision of Himachal Pradesh State Commission in
Life Insurance Corporation of India Vs Sheetla Devi I
(2011) CPJ 128 & decision of Uttarakhand State Commission in
Life Insurance Corporation of India Vs Bina Joshi I
(2010) CPJ 77.
9.                The complainant has filed her affidavit along with a set of documents including medical prescription, hospital papers, death certificate and discharge summary which are at page 37 to 110. The opposite party no.1-financer has filed affidavit of Rajesh Chouhan. On behalf of opposite party no.2-insurance company an affidavit of Abhishek Dadli along with documents including policy and proposal form which are at page no.111 to 133.
10.              We have carefully perused the record as also the impugned order. On perusal of the record we find that it is an admitted fact that the deceased-insured had obtained two policies in order to secure his loan amount taken from the financer. It is also admitted that the deceased-
-7-
insured died on 15.05.2017 due to kidney failure even after having underwent kidney transplant. It is also true that the insurance company repudiated the death claim of deceased-insured filed by the complainant on the ground of suppression of pre-existing disease i.e. hypertension. The insurance company relied upon one medical prescription of Dr. Suman Agrawal dated 08.08.2016 (at page 55) and not on the other prescription of the same doctor dated 08.08.2016 (at page 56).  It is also clear from paragraph 7(5) at page 5 of the reply of the insurance company wherein the insurance company denied the allegations that on 11.01.2017 two persons from the insurance company came and advise her to give in writing to the effect that the deceased-insured was suffering from pre-existing disease i.e. hypertension in order to get claim amount at the earliest and they also managed the Dr. Suman Agrawal to write hypertension on the prescription and took Rs.25,000/- from her for settling the claim at the earliest.
11.              We have perused both the prescriptions given by Dr. Suman Agrawal dated 08.08.2016 which are at page 55 and 56 respectively, very minutely and found that in the prescription dated 08.08.2016 (at page 55) between complaint and prescription of medicines in the blank space it has been written 'complaint of HT since last 4-5 years'. Same prescription of Dr. Suman Agrawal dated 08.08.2016 which is at page 56, there is no mention with regard to 'Hypertension'. Therefore, we find that the prescriptions given
-8-
by Dr. Suman Agrawal appears to be suspicious as in one prescription he has made an observation regarding hypertension and in the other there is no observation of hypertension.  It is well settled principle that if the insurance company had taken ground of hypertension i.e. pre-existing disease for repudiation of the claim, it is the duty of the insurance company as also burden lies on it to prove by cogent evidence that the prescription of Dr. Suman Agrawal at page 55 is genuine and at 56 is false.
12.              In aforesaid regard, the insurance company has also failed to produce evidence in form of the affidavit of Dr. Suman Agrawal to the effect that the deceased-insured was suffering from hypertension or not, more particularly when he had given contradictory prescriptions. It is not in dispute that no affidavit by the concerned doctor was filed whose prescriptions have been filed. Even otherwise, nexus between the alleged illness of the deceased-insured and cause of death has not at all been established.
13.              It is also pertinent to mention here that on 26.06.2023, time was sought on behalf of appellant to file medical literature in order to substantiate that hypertension is a cause of kidney failure but learned counsel failed to file the same on record.
14.              In the discharge summary dated 15.05.2017 of Choithram Hospital & Research Centre, Indore, (at page 67) there is no mention of any complaint of hypertension.
-9-
15.              The insurance company has filed proposal form which is at page 132-133. On bare perusal of the said proposal form we find that there are no interrogatories or questionnaire with regard to health status. If the interrogatories/questionnaire in the proposal form has any bearing on acceptance or rejection of the proposal then the said information should also be significant in taking a decision as to whether the risk was bad or not. Here in the instant matter there are no queries. In such circumstances, it cannot be said that the complainant knowingly suppressed the material information with regard to any disease while filling up the proposal form in order to obtain the insurance policy. The judgments relied upon by learned counsel for the appellant are on different facts and circumstances and are not applicable in the present matter.
16.              Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.8245 of 2015 (
Sulbha Prakash Motegaonkar & Ors Vs Life Insurance Corporation of India
) decided on 05.10.2015 has held that "It is not the case of the insurance company that the ailment that the deceased was suffering from was a life threatening disease which could or did cause the death of the insured.  In fact, the clear case is that the deceased died due to ischemic heart disease and also because of myocardial infarction.  The concealment of lumbar spondylitis with PID with sciatica persuaded the respondent not to grant the insurance claim. We are of the opinion that National
-10-
Commission was in error in denying to the appellants the insurance claim and accepting the repudiation of the claim by the respondent. The death of the insured due to ischemic heart disease and myocardial infarction had nothing to do with this lumbar spondylitis with PID with sciatica.  In our considered opinion, since the alleged concealment was not such a nature as would disentitle the deceased from getting his life insured, the repudiation of the claim was incorrect and not justified."
17.              From the above observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is clear that suppression of any information relating to pre-existing disease if it has not resulted in death or has no direct relationship to cause of death, would not completely disentitle the claimant for the claim. Even otherwise, the insurance claim cannot be denied on the ground of life style diseases that are so common.
18.              In view of the aforesaid discussion and keeping in view the facts, and circumstances of the case, we find that there is no cogent, convincing and reliable evidence on record to prove that there was material concealment of facts on part of the deceased-insured and as such there are no reasons to interfere with the order of the District Commission and same is upheld by dismissing the appeal. There is no order as to costs.
(A. K. Tiwari)                          (Dr. Srikant Pandey)

 

            Presiding Member                             Member
